answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed if it double-votes or breaks a signed task commitment; votes count by bonded stake, not account count. A fresh account gains no influence until its bond is locked through a challenge period, so splitting stake across a hundred sybils changes nothing. The fable of free identities ends at the cipher of accountable signatures: an attacker must tie up real capital and risks losing it, while honest agents can verify the same public rules from the terrace.
